Razor Blades.body: Consider wrapping item with protective material (e.g. fabric, thick plastic) before placing in the Garbage Bin . Locations that generate a large amount of razor blades, like personal service settings, must dispose of razor blades in a sharps container, as per Ontario Regulation 136/18, personal service settings . For more information on Toronto Public Health’s safety program, please visit BodySafe .

Depot (railway ties).body: This item is not collected at curbside. If less than 1.2 meters (4 feet) in length, item can be taken to one of the City's Drop-Off Depots. If longer than 1.2 meters (4 feet), make arrangements with private company specializing in disposing of this type of waste.

Oversized (tie into rolls).body: Please tie into rolls measuring no longer than 1.2 metres (4 ft) and weighing less than 20 kilograms (44 lbs). Place item at the curb on your regular garbage collection day, 0.5 metre (2 feet) away from your Garbage Bin.

Garbage or Donate CED (books).body: Consider donating books that are in good condition to non-profit organizations or bringing to a Community Environment Day . Alternatively, place this item in the Garbage Bin .

Metal Items (remove doors from appliance.body: Please place large metal household appliance right at your curbside on your scheduled Garbage Bin collection day. For safety reasons, please remove doors from fridges, freezers, ovens and other large appliances. Please set out appliance and door(s) for pick up 0.5 metre (2 feet) away from your Garbage Bin.

Garbage (wrapping and tying).body: Place item in the Garbage Bin.

Oversized (donate or empty).body: Consider donating reusable items. Alternatively, place item at the curb on your regular garbage collection day, 0.5 metre (2 feet) away from your Garbage Bin. Residents of apartments/condos should take electronics to their building’s designated drop-off area.

HHW (fertilizers, pesticides, herbicides.body: This item is Household Hazardous Waste (HHW) and MUST NOT be placed in the garbage, Blue Bin (recycling), Green Bin (organics) or put down the drain, toilet or sewer. Please take this item to one of the City's Drop-Off Depots or Community Environment Days . For HHW between 10 to 50 litres/kilograms, you can request a free Toxic Taxi pickup online or by calling 311. In an apartment/condo, building staff need to request pickup. For more drop-off locations check https://www.productcare.org/products/hhw/ontario/ .

For safe storage, place used batteries back in their original packaging or cover the positive terminal with clear packing tape, duct tape or electrical tape or place in a clear plastic bag (wrap multiple batteries together). In an apartment or condo building, pickup needs to be arranged by building staff.

If you live in a multi-residential building, please take this item to your building’s designated area for oversized items.

Yard Waste (emerald ash borer beetle).body: All wood waste, including that which is suffering from the emerald ash borer beetle, can be put to the curb as long as it does not exceed 7.5 cm (3 inches) in diameter. If items exceed 7.5 cm (3 inches) in diameter, please make arrangements with a private company specializing in handling this type of waste.

Garland.body: Remove all decorations before placing this item out as Yard Waste. Place this item in a kraft paper yard waste bag, yard waste bin, or any open top, rigid reusable container with handles. This item may be taken to a Drop-Off Depot when Yard Waste collection is not available.

Donate (NOT CED) or Garbage (miscellaneo.body: Consider donating reusable items. Alternatively, this item should be placed in the Garbage Bin .

Depot (construction & renovation waste -.body: This item is not collected curbside. Take this item for disposal as garbage to one of the City's Drop-Off Depots . Disposal fees may apply.

Green Bin (cereal, grains & baked goods).body: Place this item in the Green Bin.

Donate (incl. CED) or Garbage (school/of.body: Consider donating reusable items. Some items can also be dropped off for reuse at Community Environment Days . Alternatively, this item should be placed in the Garbage Bin.

HHW (empty paint cans).body: This item is Household Hazardous Waste (HHW) and MUST NOT be disposed of in the garbage, Blue Bin (recycling), Green Bin (organics), drain, toilet or sewer. Please take this item to one of the City's Drop-Off Depots or Community Environment Days . For HHW between 10 to 50 litres/kilograms, residents can request a free Toxic Taxi pick-up online or by calling 311. In an apartment/condo, building staff need to request pickup.

Not Accepted (Large dead animal).body: If you find an injured or dead animal, please contact 311 . If found dead on private property, skunks, raccoons, opossums and unowned domestic animals need to be bagged and placed at the curb for pickup, but coyotes and deer do not need to be. You can also make an appointment to bring dead animals to a Toronto Animal Shelter for disposal. If the dead animal is under a deck or porch, please call a private company for animal removal.

Oversized (drain fuel first).body: Drain all fuel and dispose of it as Household Hazardous Waste . Place this item at your curb on your regular garbage collection day, 0.5 metre (2 feet) away from your Garbage Bin.

Solar lamps - remove batteries.body: Remove any batteries and dispose of them as Household Hazardous Waste . Place this item in the Garbage Bin .

HHW (containers, even if empty).body: This item is Household Hazardous Waste (HHW), even if empty, and MUST NOT be placed in the Garbage Bin, Blue Bin or Green Bin. Take this item to one of the City's Drop-Off Depots or Community Environment Days . For HHW between 10 and 50 litres/kilograms, you can request a free Toxic Taxi pickup online or by calling 311.

Not accepted (Guns, bullets, explosives).body: This type of waste is not accepted by the City of Toronto. If you find this item and it’s an emergency, call 911. If you’re turning it in, call the Toronto police non-emergency line at 416-808-2222. Do not take item to a police station.

HHW (gasoline).body: This item is Household Hazardous Waste (HHW) and MUST NOT be placed in the Garbage Bin, Blue Bin, Green Bin or put down the drain, toilet or sewer. Please take this item to one of the City's Drop-Off Depots or Community Environment Days . It must be brought in any container that has a lid, is securely closed and can be left behind. For HHW between 10 to 50 litres/kilograms, you can request a free Toxic Taxi pickup online or by calling 311.

Green Bin - if soiled w chem, then garba.body: Place this item in the Green Bin . If soiled with chemicals such as cleaning products, place in the Garbage Bin.

Oversized (no special instructions).body: Place this item at the curb on your regular garbage collection day, 0.5 metre (2 feet) away from your Garbage Bin. If you live in a multi-residential building, please take this item to your building’s designated area for oversized items.

HHW (batteries - no prep).body: This item is Household Hazardous Waste (HHW) and MUST NOT be disposed of in the garbage, Blue Bin (recycling) or Green Bin (organics). In an apartment or condo building, pickup needs to be arranged by building staff.

Garbage (invasive plants).body: All invasive plants should be bagged and placed in the Garbage Bin to prevent spread.

Green Bin - tampons.body: Place plastic wrappers and applicators in the garbage . Place tampons in the Green Bin (organics) . If you have received treatment involving radioactivity, please contact the location where you received treatment for advice on how to safely dispose of items soiled with bodily fluids.

Take this item to any pharmacy, or one of the City's Drop-Off Depots or Community Environment Days . For HHW between 10 to 50 litres/kilograms, residents can also request a free Toxic Taxi pick-up online or by calling 311. In an apartment/condo, building staff need to request pickup.

Drywall.body: This item is not collected at curbside. Clean construction drywall, including painted, papered or vinyl covered, is accepted at certain Drop-Off Depots (Bermondsey, Commissioners, Ingram).

Garbage (matches, sparklers).body: Soak thoroughly in water, then wrap in double plastic bags (to keep them from drying out) before placing in the Garbage Bin .

Garbage (ashes).body: Place this cooled item in the Garbage Bin.

paper muffin/cupcake wrappers.body: If waxed or made of parchment paper, place in the Garbage Bin . Otherwise, place this item in the Green Bin .

soiled pizza box.body: Remove any plastic pieces and place those in the Garbage Bin . Place this item in the Green Bin .

Green Bin (non-paper tea bags).body: Open bag and empty tea into Green Bin . Place bag in Garbage Bin .

Garbage (cigarette).body: Place this extinguished and cooled item in the Garbage Bin.

Green Bin (food-soiled bags w/ handles).body: Remove any non-paper handles and components (e.g. ribbons, rope, grommets) and place those in the Garbage Bin. If lined with plastic (can be revealed by ripping slowly), then place in the Garbage Bin. Otherwise, place this item in the Green Bin .

Garbage (fireworks).body: Completely submerge fireworks in water and soak them overnight. Place the soaked fireworks in the garbage . Dispose of fireworks in small quantities (up to 10 items).

Not accepted (Soil).body: Soil from excavation, landscaping, etc. is not accepted by the City of Toronto. Only small amounts of soil from indoor plants can be placed in the Green Bin (organics). Please make arrangements with a private company to dispose of this item.

HHW (CFL, fluorescent lights, excl tubes.body: These contain mercury and MUST be disposed of as Household Hazardous Waste (HHW) . Place in original box or bundle/tape together in groups of 8. Take these to one of the City's Drop-Off Depots or Community Environment Days or a retailer that accepts lighting. For HHW between 10 to 50 litres/kilograms, you can request a free Toxic Taxi pickup online or by calling 311. In an apartment/condo, building staff need to request pickup.
